prose.label: Order inside the firewall module.
prose.text: Evaluation order among the firewall policies is open {{gap:module-internal-order}}. The web side is covered in [[zia.url-filtering]] and [[zia.ssl-inspection.pipeline]], and Cloud App Control in [[zia.cloud-app-control.precedence]].

checks.do: Whether the location has the firewall enabled, since enforcement depends on it.
Whether the traffic is Z-Tunnel 1.0 or PAC, and the option to enable the firewall for it is on.
Whether the block appears in both logs, which marks a firewall block, or only in Web Insights, which marks a web-policy block.
Whether the web-rule attribution fields settle a disagreement between the firewall log and Web Insights.

firewall-first.statement: All web traffic is evaluated in the firewall module first, and only traffic that does not violate a firewall policy is forwarded to the web module.

quotes: All web traffic is first evaluated in the Firewall module and only if it passes the Firewall module (i.e., if it didn't violate any Firewall policies), it's forwarded to the web module where the traffic is evaluated against the Web policies.

nonweb-firewall-only.statement: Outbound traffic to ports other than 80/443 (or other HTTP or HTTPS ports) goes directly to the firewall module and is blocked if it violates a firewall policy.

quotes: Outbound non-web traffic: When the Public Service Edge receives outbound non-web traffic going to ports other than 80/443 (or other HTTP or HTTPS ports), it sends the traffic directly to the Firewall module for policy evaluation. If the traffic violates a Firewall policy, it blocks the transaction.

firewall-beats-web-allow.statement: If a web policy allows a transaction but a conflicting firewall policy blocks it, the firewall policy applies: for example, Cloud App Control allowing Box.com does not help when the firewall blocks it.

quotes: If your organization's Web policy allows a transaction but has a conflicting Firewall policy that blocks it, the service applies the Firewall policy. For example, if the web Cloud App Control policy allows the application Box.com, but the Firewall policy blocks it, the service blocks the transaction.

enforcement-conditions.statement: The firewall module enforces on web traffic only when the traffic is outbound, from the user to the web, and the organization has enabled a firewall policy for the location.

quotes: The following conditions must be true for the policy enforcement for web traffic in the Firewall module. If these conditions are met, the Firewall module enforces policies on web traffic:
The traffic is outbound, going from the user to the web.
The organization has enabled a Firewall policy for the location.

explicit-forwarding-tuples.statement: For remote users on explicit forwarding, the firewall evaluates both the inner and the outer tuples.

quotes: For remote users using explicit forwarding traffic, Zscaler evaluates both the inner and outer tuples.

firewall-block-both-logs.statement: When web traffic violates a firewall policy, both the Firewall Insights and Web Insights logs show it blocked.

quotes: When the web traffic violates a Firewall policy, both the Firewall and the Web Insights Logs indicate that the traffic is blocked.

web-block-firewall-allowed.statement: When traffic passes the firewall policy but violates a web policy, Firewall Insights shows it allowed and Web Insights shows it blocked.

quotes: However, if the traffic passes the Firewall policy but violates a Web policy, the Firewall Insights Logs indicate that the traffic is allowed, whereas the Web Insights Logs indicate it as blocked.

firewall-log-action.statement: The firewall NSS feed records the action as Allowed or Blocked, and the name of the rule applied to the transaction.

quotes: | The action that the service took on the transaction: Allowed or Blocked
| The name of the rule that was applied to the transaction

ztunnel-pac-opt-in.statement: For Z-Tunnel 1.0 and PAC traffic, the firewall must be enabled in Advanced Settings for this type of traffic: the option is Enable Firewall for Z-Tunnel 1.0 and PAC Road Warriors.

quotes: If your organization uses Z-Tunnel 1.0 or PAC files to route traffic, ensure that the firewall is enabled for this type of traffic in the Advanced Settings.
you must enable the Enable Firewall for Z-Tunnel 1.0 and PAC Road Warriors option
If your organization uses Zscaler Tunnel (Z-Tunnel) 1.0 or PAC files to route traffic, ensure that the firewall is enabled for this type of traffic in the Advanced Settings.

extends-to-proxy-traffic.statement: Firewall Filtering rules can be extended to traffic managed by the web proxy in specific cases: when the rules contain Layer 3, Layer 4 or FQDN conditions, or when non-web traffic appears in flows managed by the web proxy. Rules based on source IP address, destination IP address or destination FQDN apply to proxy-managed traffic in both Standard and Advanced Firewall, while handing non-web traffic over from the web proxy to the firewall needs Advanced Firewall; the page's example is SSH on destination port 443.

quotes: Firewall Filtering rules can also be extended to traffic managed by the web proxy in specific cases when the rules contain Layer 3 or Layer 4 or FQDN conditions or when non-web traffic appears in flows managed by the web proxy.
Extend the Firewall Filtering policy to traffic managed by web proxy using rules configured based on source IP address, destination IP address, or destination FQDN.
This is supported in Standard and Advanced Firewall.
Extend the Firewall Filtering policy to non-web traffic handed over to firewall by the web proxy with Advanced Firewall.

For example, with Advanced Firewall, if SSH (non-web traffic) uses destination port 443 (typically a secure web traffic port), the web proxy hands over that traffic to the firewall for full non-web identification and policy application.

web-bypass-identification.statement: Identifying web traffic that is bypassing the web proxy and forwarding it to the web proxy for policy application needs Advanced Firewall and auto-proxy configuration in the Advanced Settings.

quotes: Identify web traffic that is bypassing the web proxy and forward it to the web proxy for policy application with Advanced Firewall. This requires auto-proxy configuration in the Advanced Settings.

recommended-connectivity.statement: Zscaler recommends GRE or IPSec tunnel connectivity from branch or headquarter location gateway devices, and installing Zscaler Client Connector for remote users to connect to the Zscaler service. Zscaler Client Connector should be implemented when users are off network using HTTP CONNECT tunnels to forward their traffic.

quotes: Zscaler recommends using GRE/IPSec tunnel connectivity from branch or headquarter location gateway devices. For remote users, the recommendation is to install Zscaler Client Connector to connect to the Zscaler service.
Zscaler Client Connector should be implemented when users are off network using HTTP CONNECT tunnels to forward their traffic.

connect-inner-outer.statement: With HTTP CONNECT tunnels, there are two 5-tuples associated with the traffic, the outer IP and the inner IP address. Zscaler removes the HTTP CONNECT request from the outer tunnel and applies the Firewall policies to the request inside the tunnel independently, so any 5-tuple that results in a blocking policy blocks the corresponding session.

quotes: With HTTP CONNECT tunnels, there are two 5-tuples associated with the traffic: the outer IP and the inner IP address.

Zscaler removes the HTTP CONNECT request from the outer tunnel and then applies the Firewall policies to the request inside the HTTP CONNECT tunnel independently. This means that any 5-tuple that results in a blocking policy blocks the corresponding session.

proxy-connectivity-objects.statement: To allow connectivity to the Zscaler service, an organization's policies must use three predefined objects: the Zscaler Proxy Network Service, which includes all proxied network services (for example TCP 21, 80, 443, 9400, 9480) and the subscription to a DPPC port; the Zscaler Proxy IPs IP category, which includes all Public Service Edge service IPs in a particular cloud, the Public Service Edge's local IPs and global service IPs; and the Zscaler Proxy Traffic Firewall policy rule, which matches that category and that service. Zscaler Client Connector version 2.0 or later uses DTLS/TLS tunnels to forward traffic and does not support the Zscaler Proxy Traffic rule.

quotes: To ensure your organization is configured to allow connectivity to the Zscaler service, you must leverage the following predefined Zscaler network services and IP groups in your organization’s policies:
A predefined network service: Zscaler Proxy Network Service - This includes all proxied network services (e.g., TCP 21, 80, 443, 9400, 9480, etc.) and the subscription to a DPPC port.

A predefined IP category: Zscaler Proxy IPs - It includes all Public Service Edge for Internet & SaaS (ZIA) service IPs in a particular cloud, local IPs of the particular Public Service Edge for Internet & SaaS, and global service IPs.
A predefined Firewall policy rule: Zscaler Proxy Traffic - This is available to match the Zscaler Proxy IPs category and the Zscaler Proxy Networking Service.
Zscaler Client Connector version 2.0 or later uses DTLS/TLS tunnels to forward traffic, and it doesn't support Zscaler Proxy Traffic rule.

alg.statement: Some protocols currently cannot be fully handled by Public Service Edges and require an application layer gateway (ALG) feature to be tracked across control and bearer channels; the Zscaler service applies the ALG feature automatically to the protocols the page lists: FTP (passive), PPTP and RTSP. Traffic for protocols that are not fully supported by an ALG, like SIP, H.323, H.248, VOIP and TFTP, might need to be bypassed from Zscaler by changing the configuration when setting up forwarding methods such as IPSec, GRE or Z-Tunnel 2.0 (for remote users). The page says the best practice for those forwarding methods is generally to send all ports and protocols through the tunnels.

quotes: The best practice for customers using forwarding methods such as IPSec, GRE, or Zscaler Tunnel (Z-Tunnel) 2.0 (for remote users) is generally to send all ports and protocols through their tunnels.

However, there are some protocols that currently cannot be fully handled by Public Service Edges for Internet & SaaS (ZIA). These protocols require an application layer gateway (ALG) feature to be tracked across control and bearer channels.
The Zscaler service supports and applies the ALG feature automatically to the following protocols: - FTP (passive) - PPTP - RTSP

Traffic forwarded to the protocols that are not fully supported by an ALG (like SIP, H.323, H.248, VOIP, and TFTP) might need to be bypassed from Zscaler by changing the configuration when setting up your forwarding methods such as IPSec, GRE, or Z-Tunnel 2.0 (for remote users).

ztunnel1-pac-rules.statement: Enabling the Enable Firewall for Z-Tunnel 1.0 and PAC Road Warriors option applies the following Firewall rules to remote user traffic forwarded via Z-Tunnel 1.0 or PAC: all the default Firewall rules, all the user-defined rules configured without any location criteria, and all the user-defined rules configured for the Road Warrior location, because Road Warrior applies only to Z-Tunnel 2.0 when the option is disabled. The page says to ensure these rules are relevant for Z-Tunnel 1.0 and PAC traffic before enabling it.

quotes: Enable Firewall for Z-Tunnel 1.0 and PAC Road Warriors: Enabling the option applies the following Firewall rules to the remote user traffic forwarded via Z-Tunnel 1.0 or PAC:
All the default Firewall rules.
All the user-defined rules configured without any location criteria.
All the user-defined rules configured for the Road Warrior location because Road Warrior applies only to Z-Tunnel 2.0 when this option is disabled.
Ensure that these Firewall rules are relevant for the traffic forwarded via Z-Tunnel 1.0 and PAC before enabling this option.

inbound-web-module-only.statement: Inbound web traffic (HTTP or HTTPS on ports 80/443 from the internet in response to GET or POST requests) is sent to the web module for policy evaluation, and is allowed into the organization if it violates no Web policy.

quotes: When the Public Service Edge receives inbound web traffic (HTTP or HTTPS traffic for ports 80/443) from the internet in response to HTTP GET or POST requests, it sends the traffic to its web module for policy evaluation.
If the traffic does not violate any Web policies, it allows the traffic into your organization.

web-block-firewall-log-conflict.title: Does the firewall log show a web-module block as allowed or blocked
web-block-firewall-log-conflict.detail: The policy-enforcement guide says Firewall Insights shows traffic that passes the firewall but violates a web policy as allowed. Later, for HTTP traffic, it says that when the web module blocks a transaction the Public Service Edge does not send the traffic to the firewall module, 'However, your Firewall logs show that the user's web transaction is blocked.' The two statements are in the same guide and are not reconciled.
web-block-firewall-log-conflict.blocks: using the firewall log action alone to tell a firewall block from a web block

quotes: However, your Firewall logs show that the user's web transaction is blocked.

module-internal-order.title: Evaluation order among Filtering, NAT, DNS, IPS and FTP
module-internal-order.detail: The old reference asserted both a fixed sequence (Filtering, NAT, DNS, IPS, FTP) and, separately, that NAT Control evaluates before Firewall Filtering, and that a flow traverses all four with a block from any dropping it. No captured source states an order or a traversal rule among the firewall policies. The only ordering stated is that ATP rules evaluate before IPS Control rules.
module-internal-order.blocks: answering whether a NAT rewrite changes what Filtering sees

ztunnel-2-firewall.title: Whether Z-Tunnel 2.0 engages the firewall without an option
ztunnel-2-firewall.detail: The old reference said Z-Tunnel 2.0 forwarding engages the firewall automatically and that without the opt-in the firewall and IPS never run on Z-Tunnel 1.0 and PAC traffic. The captures only say the firewall must be enabled for Z-Tunnel 1.0 and PAC; the Advanced Settings page adds that Road Warrior applies only to Z-Tunnel 2.0 when the option is disabled (ztunnel1-pac-rules), but does not say the firewall engages Z-Tunnel 2.0 automatically.
ztunnel-2-firewall.blocks: explaining why firewall rules do or do not apply to a forwarding method
